title: The summary for Friday 20 November
text:
Good morning, it is Friday 20 November: this is the GERICO summary.

I begin with Kyiv. Overnight, a Russian missile and drone attack struck three bridges over the Dnipro. Mayor Vitali Klitschko speaks of three dead and about fifteen injured, according to Reuters. Putin had promised a response to the Ukrainian attack on the Crimean bridge.

On the Shenzhen summit: the trilateral meeting between Trump, Xi and Putin ended with a four-point statement and no concrete agreements, writes Il Post. On Ukraine, the Kremlin and Kyiv give different versions.

In the Middle East, the Saudi-led coalition says it intercepted a Houthi ballistic missile headed towards the south of the kingdom. On Thursday, a Houthi attack damaged the headquarters of the sovereign wealth fund in Riyadh.

In Italy, today there is a general strike by the CGIL against the budget, with marches in about one hundred cities. Planes and trains are excluded, but trains stop from 21:00 due to a strike by other trade unions.

In business, Unicredit and the German government have reached an agreement in principle on Commerzbank: the headquarters in Frankfurt and the listing remain. Still on banks, the Financial Times writes that the Italian branch of Deutsche Bank allegedly concealed losses of up to 800 million euros. The bank replies that the accounts were correct and that the auditor did not ask for adjustments.

Moving on to the markets. Wall Street closed sharply lower on Thursday, for the sixth consecutive session. The Dow Jones loses 2.19 per cent and falls below fifty thousand points. The S&P 500 sheds 2.02 per cent, the Nasdaq 2.25. Al Jazeera links the decline to fears over an artificial intelligence bubble. Anthropic stock made its debut and closed 17 per cent above the offer price, at 97 dollars.

This morning Asia is sharply down. During the session, Tokyo's Nikkei loses up to 4.9 per cent, Seoul's Kospi 5.4 and Taipei's Taiex over 6.8. These are mid-session values, not closing prices.

In Europe on Thursday, Piazza Affari closed down by 0.46 per cent, London by 0.9. The spread between BTPs and Bunds is at 107 basis points. European gas rises by 4 per cent, to 84 euros per megawatt-hour.

On gold, oil and exchange rates, today's sources do not provide verified data, so I am not reporting them.

Today's events. At a quarter past nine, ECB President Lagarde speaks. At twenty-five past fourteen, Fed Governor Waller speaks. At sixteen o'clock, eurozone consumer confidence and the University of Michigan consumer sentiment are released.

The full news, with sources, is on GERICO. No investment advice.
